$comment: Machine-readable task list for this kit. An agent should read AGENTS.md first, then work this file in `order`. Every patch has a `verify` check id that scripts/check-seo.mjs reports on.
constraints: ZERO design change. No patch may alter a rendered pixel. See VERIFY.md.
Patch 02 is the only one that touches the DOM; it adds sr-only elements and modifies no existing element.
Do not add FAQPage schema. Google restricted FAQ rich results to government and health sites in 2023.
Do not apply patch 08 without a human answering its blocking question first.
Never hardcode a benchmark record number. Wire it to live data or omit it.
Patch 11 is bidirectional: every spoke links to quantum.starkware.co AND the hub links back to the spokes. Adding only inbound links to the hub makes the spokes invisible and undoes patch 10.

patches.title: Dataset, WebPage and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD
patches.action: Copy JsonLd.tsx into the qsb route directory and render <QsbJsonLd /> inside the page component, passing the live record values as props.
patches.acceptance: curl -sL https://www.yukon.org/qsb | grep -c 'application/ld+json' returns >= 1, and the JSON parses with a Dataset node.
patches.notes: Renders no DOM. Pass live records as props; do not hardcode.

patches.title: sr-only h2 heading outline
patches.action: Add one <h2 className="sr-only"> as the first child of each <section> and each tab panel. Use the question-shaped wording from patches/09-aeo (fix 2), not the plain labels.
patches.acceptance: curl -sL https://www.yukon.org/qsb | grep -o '<h2' | wc -l returns >= 2, and a screenshot diff against the pre-change page is pixel-identical.
patches.notes: Do NOT retag the existing section labels. They are <button> tab controls and a nav <a>; retagging breaks role=tab and changes design. Add new elements only.

patches.title: robots.txt
patches.action: Add app/robots.ts at the app root. Use the static public/robots.txt variant instead if the project prefers it, never both.
patches.acceptance: https://www.yukon.org/robots.txt returns 200 with content-type text/plain and contains a Sitemap: line.
patches.notes: Site-wide, not QSB-specific. Currently 404s as an HTML soft-404.

patches.title: sitemap.xml
patches.action: Add app/sitemap.ts. Replace the hardcoded CHALLENGES array with the app's existing source of truth for open challenges.
patches.acceptance: https://www.yukon.org/sitemap.xml returns 200 with an XML content-type.
patches.notes: Site-wide. A stale hand-maintained sitemap is worse than none, so generate it.

patches.title: llms.txt
patches.notes: Community convention with no confirmed vendor support. Genuinely optional. Skipping costs nothing measurable.

patches.title: longer title and meta description
patches.action: Replace the exported metadata object with the one in metadata.ts.
patches.acceptance: Rendered <title> is 50-60 chars; meta description is >= 150 chars.
patches.notes: Changes the browser tab text. That is the only user-visible difference in this entire kit, and it is not page design. The og:site_name change is a branding call for a human, not an automatic edit.

patches.title: qsb.fast redirect 307 to 308
patches.human_question: Is the qsb.fast alias configured in the Vercel dashboard or in vercel.json? The dashboard route needs a human with project access.
patches.action: Set the qsb.fast domain redirect to permanent (308), and point it directly at https://www.yukon.org/qsb to collapse both hops into one.
patches.acceptance: curl -sI https://qsb.fast returns 308 with location https://www.yukon.org/qsb.
patches.notes: Most likely a dashboard toggle, no deploy needed.

patches.title: cache headers on a public page
patches.human_question: Does /qsb render anything that differs per viewer, for example a signed-in solver's own row? If yes, no-store may be correct and the leaderboard should be cached separately instead.
patches.action: DO NOT APPLY until the human question above is answered. If the page is identical for all anonymous visitors, add `export const revalidate = 60`. If it is per-viewer, cache the leaderboard segment separately instead.
patches.acceptance: cache-control on the document no longer contains no-store, and median full response drops below 800ms.
patches.notes: Largest speed lever available, and the only patch that can be wrong to apply.

patches.title: answer engine optimization
patches.action: Apply fixes 1 to 4 and 7 in patches/09-aeo/README.md. Fix 5 is a one-line edit to a DIFFERENT repository and needs no deploy; do it first.
patches.acceptance: Page contains a single self-contained sentence stating the current record, a visible or sr-only 'verified as of' timestamp, and the JSON-LD carries dateModified plus a numeric variableMeasured value.
patches.notes: Evidence: on 2026-09-18 an answer engine cited the GitHub repo rather than this page, and quoted 233,402,654 as the record when the live record was 726,763,328. Fix 6 is off-site work for a human, not an engineering task.

patches.title: rank for the quantum safe bitcoin head term
patches.human_question: Who owns starkware.co/blog? Fix 1 is a one-paragraph edit to a StarkWare blog post, not a code change, and needs whoever publishes that blog.
patches.action: Fix 1: add a link to qsb.fast from starkware.co's quantum-safe-bitcoin blog post, which ranks #1 for the target query and currently links nowhere near the benchmark. Fix 2a: make the transaction cost figure self-contained and dated on the page. Fix 2b (human, not engineering): brief the outlets that published the $200 figure.
patches.acceptance: starkware.co blog post contains a link to qsb.fast, and the /qsb page states the current cost with a verified-as-of date in extractable prose.
patches.notes: Do NOT chase the head term directly. Intent is informational and a leaderboard cannot satisfy it. Do not stuff 'quantum bitcoin' into the title, and do not build a competing what-is explainer: it would compete with StarkWare's own #1 result. Evidence in the patch README.

patches.title: route the post-quantum cluster through quantum.starkware.co
patches.human_question: Two owners are outside the QSB codebase. Who publishes quantum.starkware.co (PMM team) and who can approve an outbound link from www.yukon.org/qsb to a StarkWare domain?
patches.action: Build a bidirectional hub-and-spoke: the hub links out to the starkware.co blog post and qsb.fast; both spokes link back to the hub. Vary anchor text. Then give the hub the same JSON-LD and heading treatment as patches 01 and 02.
patches.acceptance: All three checks in the patch README return a match: hub contains qsb.fast, blog post contains quantum.starkware.co, qsb.fast contains quantum.starkware.co. All three return nothing today.
patches.notes: Do NOT make links one-directional into the hub. Authority flows the way links point; inbound-only makes the hub rank and leaves the spokes invisible, which undoes patch 10. The hub already has robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt (ahead of yukon.org) but has zero JSON-LD, 110 words and zero h2.
